_source: GOVDOCS1 (NPS/Digital Corpora file corpus): ~986,278 files (~488 GB), collected 2009-2010 by searching for random dictionary words / random numbers / combinations of both via Yahoo and Google, restricted to web servers in the .gov domain; released public-domain / freely redistributable for research. Hosted by Digital Corpora (digitalcorpora.org) on the public 'digitalcorpora' S3 bucket under the AWS Open Data Sponsorship Program since Nov 2020. Citation: Garfinkel, Farrell, Roussev & Dinolt, "Bringing Science to Digital Forensics with Standardized Forensic Corpora," DFRWS 2009, Montreal, Canada. This corpus and every entry below is disjoint by construction from manifests/respec_public_review_queue.json and manifests/respec_public_candidates.json, which are drawn from this project's own raw/docx-corpus batches, not from GOVDOCS1.
_caveat: UNVERIFIED PAST THE CONTAINER LEVEL. Real effort was made (live queries against the public 'digitalcorpora' S3 bucket's list-objects XML, plus digitalcorpora.org's own documentation and statistical-report pages) but no individually browsable GOVDOCS1 docx file index exists: the by_type/ prefix exposes exactly one object per extension (a single zip bundling every file of that extension across the whole corpus), the threads/ and zipfiles/ prefixes likewise expose only monolithic per-thread/per-shard zips (not extracted per-file listings), and digitalcorpora.org's own 'Search Govdocs1' tool returned 'the search facility is currently not working' when checked on 2026-09-27. Digital Corpora's own content-sniffed (not extension-based) statistical report counts only 164 files in the ENTIRE ~986,278-file corpus as genuine 'MS Word Documents (Open XML)'; the corpus-wide by-extension count could be higher or lower, since that same report notes 33,917 files corpus-wide carry the wrong extension for their actual content. Consequently none of the four entries below is an individual candidate document -- each is a real, verified, directly-resolving bulk container (S3 key, size, last-modified all confirmed live) plus notes on why/how to use it. No file, zip, or byte of document content was downloaded, fetched, or opened for this task -- only S3 bucket-listing XML metadata and Digital Corpora's public doc/report pages were read. Turning this into 2-3 individual eligible documents requires the separate, explicitly gated download step (this project's rule on downloading files) followed by extraction, a genuine-Open-XML sniff (corpus mislabels extensions), and this repo's own tools/respec_eligibility.py structural check.
_eligibility_target: Per tools/respec_eligibility.py's docstring and manifests/respec_public_review_queue.json's own 'K=4 band' usage: keep documents with a real heading outline of roughly 3-25 headings (not the 30-100+ seen in this project's own >25-heading pool) and at least one 'usable' resolve_respec_schedule anchor-set (five-family; six-family additionally needs a disjoint table-anchor pool entry at the same index) -- i.e. favor short-to-medium structured reports/memos over omnibus documents or single-page forms.
_strategy: Recommended pipeline once the user authorizes an actual download: (1) fetch by_type/docx.zip only (29,033,269 bytes) -- the smallest bulk object and the only one pre-filtered by extension, versus a 250MB-1GB+ unfiltered thread/shard zip; (2) extract and discard extension-mislabeled impostors by checking each member is a real zip with a word/document.xml part (GOVDOCS1 is documented to mislabel extensions); (3) run this repo's existing fresh-pool pipeline (tools/scan_fresh_docx_pool.py-style outline scan, then tools/respec_eligibility.py) over the survivors and keep only the 3-25-heading, >=1-usable-anchor-set band, same as k4sr_candidates.json's own funnel; (4) if by_type/docx.zip yields fewer than 2-3 eligible documents -- plausible, since the corpus-wide content-sniffed true-docx count is only 164 and this project needs .gov-domain reports specifically -- fall back to sampling individual thread*.zip or zipfiles/NNN.zip shards (verified real examples given below) and re-running the same extension-sniff + structural filter on each extracted shard. A lower-effort way to resolve real per-file specifics (filenames, original .gov source URLs, sizes) BEFORE committing to any docx-file download is to fetch and parse the corpus root's dump.sql (298,928,989 bytes) or govdocs1-first512-first4096-docid.txt (69,584,813 bytes) -- both are structured metadata/text, not document content -- but neither was fetched in this pass because of size; doing so in a follow-up would remove the filename/URL uncertainty noted above entirely.

candidates.source_url: https://digitalcorpora.s3.amazonaws.com/corpora/files/govdocs1/by_type/docx.zip (documented front door: https://downloads.digitalcorpora.org/corpora/files/govdocs1/by_type/docx.zip, which 302-redirects to the same S3 object)
candidates.notes: PRIMARY CANDIDATE SOURCE. Verified live via S3 ListObjects XML (Last-Modified 2020-11-21T23:11:40Z, ETag 653527964512c31378d36680cb666a47-4). Bundles every file across the whole ~986,278-file corpus that carries a .docx extension -- the only by_type object that is pre-filtered to this extension. Individual member filenames/sizes are NOT visible without extracting the archive (S3 exposes only this one key, no per-file listing); expect the genuine-Open-XML yield to be a filtered subset of whatever it contains by name, since Digital Corpora's own content-sniffed report counts just 164 true 'MS Word (Open XML)' files corpus-wide. Confidence: high on the container's existence/size/URL; zero on any individual document inside it.

candidates.filename: corpora/files/govdocs1/dump.sql (root-level metadata dump, not a docx file)
candidates.notes: NOT a document -- a SQL metadata dump covering the corpus (documented per-file fields: source URL, download timestamp, search term, search engine, file length, SHA1, Dublin Core metadata). Parsing this (filtered to extension='docx') would give real filenames, original .gov source URLs and sizes without touching any document body/content, which would let a follow-up pass replace this shortlist's container-level entries with genuine individually-named candidates. Not fetched in this pass solely due to size (~299 MB); flagged here as the most promising next step for real specificity, still content-free and separate from the gated docx-file download.

Verified live via S3 listing (~322.5 MiB; one of thread0.zip..thread9.zip, each a fixed random 1000-document mutually-exclusive subset of the full corpus, documented as intended for exactly this kind of pilot sampling). Not extension-filtered -- most of its 1000 files will not be .docx -- so it is a fallback path only, listed as the 'download thread N.zip and filter' pattern in case by_type/docx.zip alone does not yield enough K=4-band-eligible .gov documents. Confidence: high on the container; zero on contents.

candidates.filename: zipfiles/000.zip (illustrative unfiltered fallback shard, alternate sharding axis)
candidates.notes: Verified live via S3 listing (zipfiles/000.zip through at least 291.zip observed, each several hundred MB to ~1 GB; this is GOVDOCS1's other documented sharding scheme -- 1000 sequential-ID-ordered bundles, versus the threads/ random-subset scheme). Also not extension-filtered. Included only to document that a second, real, differently-structured fallback path exists if both by_type/docx.zip and the threads/ sampling prove insufficient. Confidence: high on the container; zero on contents.
